title: Mitä: identifying a substance
summary: Use mitä with olla when asking what a substance is: Mitä tämä on? Mitä tämä on? — Tämä on vettä.
prerequisiteSkills: Mitä: asking and answering about actions and objects
objectives: Ask what a substance is with mitä.
Identify the substance using the singular partitive pattern.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
Use mitä with olla when asking what a substance is: Mitä tämä on? (“What is this?” about an unidentified substance). This is why mikä with olla and mitä with other verbs is not a universal rule.
keyPoints: Read the substance cue before choosing mitä; mikä would ask a different kind of identity question.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Name the substance in the singular partitive: Tämä on vettä (“This is water”). A short reply Vettä is also natural. The question is about what the material is, not how much there is or what one countable object is.
A natural short reply to “Mitä tämä on?” is “Vettä.” (“Water.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
To correct a suggested substance, reject it and name the actual substance. Both substance names keep their partitive forms in this supplied comparison.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: A substance identification answer uses the supplied partitive pattern, rather than the dictionary form.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: vettä means water here. Vesi has the irregular singular partitive vettä. Learn this common form directly.
kahvia means coffee here. Kahvi + -a gives kahvia, an unspecified amount of coffee.
mehua means juice here. Mehu + -a gives mehua.
maitoa means milk here. Maito keeps strong t and adds -a: maitoa.
teetä means tea here. Tee + -tä gives teetä, with a front-vowel ending after neutral e.
keittoa means soup here. Keitto keeps strong tt and adds -a: keittoa.
puuroa means porridge here. Puuro + -a gives puuroa.
riisiä means rice here. Riisi + -ä gives riisiä; neutral i allows the front-vowel ending.
juustoa means cheese here. Juusto + -a gives juustoa.
